That's the theme that most needs a CVD-safe alternative, and it's the default.

The form is a fill-in-the-blank passage, "Our company is … in …. We want to reach … who would pay $… per …, and we can spend $… a month on ads in …", ending in a city menu whose only city is New York; all five boroughs are mapped without being listed. The results are a map of New York's census tracts with Customers and Competitors tabs, a Gap tab once qualifying campaigns are found, a legend and clickable campaign markers at matched stations, addresses and approximate areas. Each marker shows its competitor's logo, loaded from the competitor's own website, and falls back to initials when the site's icon cannot be fetched. Solid markers identify current campaigns with a station or address match; dashed markers identify approximate, historical or undated campaigns. Markers open no popups: hovering a campaign marker highlights its row in the Competitors tab, clicking it switches to that tab and scrolls to the row, and clicking a row's location moves the map to the marker. Each mapped row shows the data-source attribution. The placements to buy are numbered markers that match their numbers in the list, shown on the Gap and Competitors layers. Without a Gap tab they also show on the Customers layer, where they are listed; with one, the Customers layer omits them. They are chosen from observed gaps when current campaign locations are available, or from audience fit otherwise. Hovering a placement on the map or in the list highlights it in both, clicking a row moves the map to it and, on phones where the map sits above the column, scrolls back up to the map, and clicking a marker scrolls the list to its row. Tabs above the results column pick the layer for both the map and the column, in the order Customers, Competitors, Gap. Gap appears only once a current campaign has a station or address match. Hovering a tract on the map names it and shows the current layer's value for it, and hovering a trait under Customers shows its exact weight in place of its measure. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Add hover values to tract boxes and trait bars`: web lint, typecheck and build passed; the hover tooltips were not checked in a browser. On the form, the whole background spins once every 30 seconds, sweeping colour through the edges the form card leaves visible, and its four coloured blobs each drift on their own loop of 7 to 10 seconds, moving up to 50% of the screen's larger side and growing by up to 40%. Reduced-motion preferences stop the spin and drift and skip the visible movement. Earlier, on 8 November 2026 in commit `Speed up gradient rotation during results transition`, desktop and 390-by-844 mobile checks showed a 1.2-second slide with no horizontal overflow. The results fill the window: the map fills the left two thirds and stays in view while the column scrolls in the right third, and on phones the map sits on top at 55% of the screen height. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Animate results upward after form submission`: desktop and 390-by-844 mobile browser checks confirmed that the results and their content move together, settle at the top without horizontal overflow, and preserve the form answers on Edit. Reduced motion completed immediately, invalid amounts blocked submission, and the browser had no console errors. Web lint, typecheck and build passed. The column opens with a one-line summary of the brief and an Edit button that brings the form back with its answers kept. Submitting a completely empty form runs the sample fintech budgeting-app brief with a $3,000 monthly budget in New York. Entering any field or changing a dropdown keeps full required-field and numeric-pattern validation. There is no separate `/map` route. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Use sample defaults for empty form submissions`: a blank submission showed the sample map and 12 placements; each individually filled field and a changed payment dropdown blocked incomplete submission; numeric patterns still blocked invalid amounts; a complete custom brief submitted its own values and Edit kept them; `/map` returned 404. The browser had no console errors, and all 26 tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. Faked: placement costs, minimum spends are invented. Real: the audience fit scores are weighted sums of the real scaled tract columns, and the placements are real kiosks and shelters selected across eligible tracts in descending observed gap-score order when current campaigns have precise locations, or descending audience fit otherwise, with one per tract and at least 500 metres between them. The column weights come from Jev through AI Gateway when `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` is set in `web/.env.local`, or on a Vercel deployment through its OIDC token: one request asks a five-level score question per column, from strongly against to strongly for, and each weight runs from -1 to 1, the probability-weighted level. Without either, or when Jev fails or takes over 20 seconds, the weights come from keyword matching on the target customer, and the Customers tab says so. Verified on 8 November 2026 with the sample brief: the Customers tab said "weighted by Jev", and the scoring request, Jev plus the tract arithmetic, took 892 ms. For "young professionals in tech who rent with roommates", the strongest weights were jobs in information (+0.94), residents aged 20 to 34 (+0.89) and median age (-0.83). Jev isn't on AI Gateway's free tier, so the key's Vercel team needs purchased AI Gateway Credits, and a card Vercel can verify. The browser computes competition per tract from its distance to each confirmed current campaign's matched station or street address, falling to about a third at 1 km, and the gap as audience fit times one minus competition; that formula is a first version, not a decision. The UI imports audience scoring, streamed competitor research and placement lookup through `web/src/lib/api.ts`, with types in `web/src/lib/contract.ts`. Placements appear after audience scoring and are re-ranked when research finishes. On 7 November 2026, the live energy-drink flow returned three competitors and three source-linked campaign findings. Their dates or station locations were unknown, so none lowered the gap scores. The production sample fallback showed three recorded competitors and its capture-date label; a different brief received no recorded findings. Both browser flows had no console errors. Verified in `2a85115`. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Show competitor logos in the list and on campaign markers`: web lint, typecheck, build and all 32 tests passed, and the logo endpoint returned a PNG for each of the sample run's three competitors. The logos were not checked in a browser. Serves G-Research and HRT.
-- Built: a settings menu (gear button, bottom right) with experimental interface options saved in the browser: sharp corners, which sets every border radius to 1px, a fade-weak-tracts switch between the quantile fade (on by default) and the earlier ramp that tints every tract, a cost-estimate switch (on by default) that shows the invented price per customer, sorts placements by it and tags the lowest, and with it off shows no prices and lists placements by area, and a colour palette choice between the default and four others that also recolour the heatmap: blue and lime (#EEF2F8 #BCCBE3 #7895C4 #33589B #14264D, accent #C6F432), purple and amber (#F2F0FB #CFC8F0 #9D8FDD #6650C2 #33228A, accent #F2A516), teal and coral (#EEF6F5 #BFE0DC #7FC2BA #2F8F86 #0B5450, accent #F2603D) and navy and amber (#F7FBFF #C7E9B4 #41B6C4 #1D91C0 #08306B, accent #FEB24C). The first four change hue along the heat ramp and their lightness peaks at the middle heat colour, so the two ends sit closer to each other in brightness than either sits to the middle; the navy palette instead darkens from #C7E9B4 to #41B6C4 to #08306B in lightness alone, and its heat-ramp separation of 31 in OKLab units barely moves under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia. Its lowest text contrast is 5.18:1, where the teal palette's is 2.72:1. Verified on 8 November 2026 in headless Chrome with both on. Navy and amber was added on 8 November 2026 at the user's request and checked by lint and typecheck only, because that session had no browser. The four older palettes are options to compare rather than agreed product decisions; navy and amber is one the user chose to add.

The first four change hue along the heat ramp and their lightness peaks at the middle heat colour, so the two ends sit closer to each other in brightness than either sits to the middle; the navy palette instead darkens from #C7E9B4 to #41B6C4 to #08306B in lightness alone, and its heat-ramp separation of 31 in OKLab units barely moves under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia. Its lowest text contrast is 5.18:1, where the teal palette's is 2.72:1. The settings menu shows "Colour-blind friendly" under the palette's name. Verified on 8 November 2026 in headless Chrome with both on. Navy and amber was added on 8 November 2026 at the user's request and checked by lint and typecheck only, because that session had no browser. The four older palettes are options to compare rather than agreed product decisions; navy and amber is one the user chose to add.
 - Built: competitor research with the Vercel AI SDK's `ToolLoopAgent`, OpenAI directly through `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and hosted web search and page reading. The research default is `gpt-5.6-luna`, selected in `AI_MODELS` in `web/src/lib/server/ai.ts`. Model names are not read from environment variables. Research runs in two stages. Discovery finds up to six competitors from the startup's product and target customer rather than its industry label: the model first writes short shopper phrases for the product and customer, then searches at least twice for companies that have run New York subway, billboard, bus shelter, LinkNYC or wild-posting campaigns and that sell a substitute or target the same customer. Government campaigns, non-profits and media owners are excluded. Discovery has eight model steps and a 45-second deadline. Each competitor then gets its own placement search for stations, street addresses and dates, with eight model steps and 65 seconds, all running concurrently within a 165-second total deadline; the Route Handler has a 170-second deadline. Each competitor can contribute up to three campaign locations, so a run reports at most 18. The first model step of each stage requires hosted search, and each response allows up to eight hosted tool calls, in parallel. Typed tools reject URLs absent from the run's research sources. Hosted-search-only responses continue into reporting within the same step budget. The model extracts the evidence; source membership does not independently fact-check its summary. Dates are classified as current, historical or unknown. Only matched subway stations or street addresses with a confirmed date range covering today affect competition. Geocoded areas and unknown or historical dates remain visible as markers without lowering gap scores. Other findings stay visible with source links, evidence and locations. A search returning no campaigns does not establish that competitors are absent. The sample recording contains three competitors and no verified campaigns. Re-capture it from `tools/` with `uv run python -c 'from tools.sources.competitor_run import load; load(refresh=True)'` while the web app runs. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Find competitors from the product and customer, then search each for placements`: live runs of four briefs each completed in 27 to 43 seconds. The dating app found Plenty of Fish, Hinge, The League, Bumble, Cerca and HUD, with 12 campaign findings, four of them at matched subway stations. The budgeting app found Openigloo, StreetEasy and Job Today; the pizza delivery service found Slice, Seamless and WoodSpoon; the telehealth service found Roman. None of the findings had confirmed current dates, so none lowered gap scores. In the browser, the sample brief listed Openigloo, StreetEasy and RentHop with seven campaign findings and no console errors. All 32 tests, web lint, typecheck and build passed. In a scratch comparison over 12 test briefs, searching named direct competitors found no campaigns at a named station or street address for any brief, and this two-stage search found them for 10 of 12. Verified earlier, on 7 November 2026 in `2a85115`: live research and production fallback flows above; eight focused tests for CSV parsing, source checks, station matching, dates, gap effects, split SDK stream chunks, interruption and cancellation; HTTP 400 for invalid briefs and 413 for oversized briefs; web lint, typecheck and build; Python Ruff checks; station data and recording present in the production deployment trace. Serves G-Research. Search and page reading alone do not establish the browser-control workflow for Wordsmith.
 - Planned: verified placement prices and minimum spends, and competitors' stores and offices as separate presence evidence. Serves G-Research and HRT. Browser control remains unbuilt for Wordsmith.
 - Built: shared model and provider setup in `web/src/lib/server/ai.ts`, using the installed SDK provider registry. Code defaults select OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna` for research and Gateway Jev for audience decisions. The research adapter bundles the model, search tool, options, credential checks, source decoding and provider errors. Unsupported research providers are rejected until a compatible search adapter is added. Model environment variables have no effect; `.env.example` lists credentials only. GPT-5.6 Luna selection was verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Use GPT-5.6 Luna for competitor research`: all 13 tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. A live smoke test returned competitor findings and streamed search progress. Verified on 7 November 2026 in `f0e401d`: all 13 focused tests passed, including registry resolution, model-environment independence, credential separation, source decoding and unsupported research-provider rejection. Web lint, typecheck and build passed. In the browser, the sample showed "weighted by Jev" and completed research with no verified competitors and no console errors while the old model variable was set to an invalid value. Serves G-Research and HRT.
 - Built: campaign location lookup with Geoapify, using `GEOAPIFY_API_KEY` on the server, and street corners from a table of New York intersections. Supported source-reported landmarks and street addresses are resolved within New York. Street corners, written as "A and B", "A & B", "A at B", "corner of A and B" or "A between B and C", are looked up in `data/streets/intersections.csv`, 55,978 intersections built by `tools/src/tools/sources/streets.py` from NYC Open Data's street centerline, and get address precision. A corner found in several boroughs is placed only when the text names one of them or a neighbourhood in it, and a corner not in the table stays unmapped; neither is sent to Geoapify, whose free-text search returned Madison Avenue & East 41st Street for "41st Street & 7th Avenue". A location naming only a borough stays unmapped. When Geoapify finds nothing for a place followed by its borough, such as "Times Square, Manhattan", it is asked again for the place alone. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Place street-corner campaigns from the city's street centerline`: 54th Street and Broadway, 14th Street and Franklin Street in Williamsburg, Sixth Avenue at Carmine Street, Lafayette and Prince Streets, and Lafayette Street between Spring and Kenmare Streets all resolved to the right corner; "41st Street and 7th Avenue" without a borough stayed unmapped; all 36 tests, web lint, typecheck and build, and the Python Ruff checks passed. Most campaign findings remain unmapped because their sources say only that the campaign ran across the subway, with no station or street. Reliable station and address matches carry their precision; broad landmarks are labelled approximate. Citywide descriptions, weak results, ambiguous alternatives and outside-city results stay unmapped with an explanation. Successful results are cached for 24 hours per server process, up to 500 entries. An unavailable key, rejected key, timeout or lookup failure preserves campaign evidence. Markers appear for known locations regardless of dates, with dashed styling for approximate, historical or undated campaigns. Clicking a marker opens the Competitors tab at its row, which shows its source, date status, location precision and attribution. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Focus campaign rows from map markers instead of popups`: with a pizza-delivery brief, clicking DoorDash's approximate Brooklyn marker from the recommendations tab switched to Competitors and highlighted its row, and clicking the row's location flew the map to the marker; the browser had no console errors, and lint, typecheck and build passed. Only current campaigns with station or street-address matches affect competition and gap scores. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Map campaign landmarks with Geoapify`: the live key resolved Times Square as approximate; the health-and-wellness flow returned Finch's Times Square billboard and displayed its undated marker and source popup on desktop and at 390 by 844 pixels. No geocoding requests appeared in browser network traffic, no API-key query strings appeared in the page, and there were no browser console errors. All 22 focused tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. Serves G-Research.

+- Built: a settings menu (gear button, bottom right) with experimental interface options saved in the browser: sharp corners, which sets every border radius to 1px, a fade-weak-tracts switch between the quantile fade (on by default) and the earlier ramp that tints every tract, a cost-estimate switch (on by default) that shows the invented price per customer, sorts placements by it and tags the lowest, and with it off shows no prices and lists placements by area, and a colour palette choice between the default and four others that also recolour the heatmap: blue and lime (#EEF2F8 #BCCBE3 #7895C4 #33589B #14264D, accent #C6F432), purple and amber (#F2F0FB #CFC8F0 #9D8FDD #6650C2 #33228A, accent #F2A516), teal and coral (#EEF6F5 #BFE0DC #7FC2BA #2F8F86 #0B5450, accent #F2603D) and navy and amber (#F7FBFF #C7E9B4 #41B6C4 #1D91C0 #08306B, accent #FEB24C). The first four change hue along the heat ramp and their lightness peaks at the middle heat colour, so the two ends sit closer to each other in brightness than either sits to the middle; the navy palette instead darkens from #C7E9B4 to #41B6C4 to #08306B in lightness alone, and its heat-ramp separation of 31 in OKLab units barely moves under simulated protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia. Its lowest text contrast is 5.18:1, where the teal palette's is 2.72:1. The settings menu shows "Colour-blind friendly" under the palette's name. Verified on 8 November 2026 in headless Chrome with both on. Navy and amber was added on 8 November 2026 at the user's request and checked by lint and typecheck only, because that session had no browser. The four older palettes are options to compare rather than agreed product decisions; navy and amber is one the user chose to add.
 - Built: competitor research with the Vercel AI SDK's `ToolLoopAgent`, OpenAI directly through `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and hosted web search and page reading. The research default is `gpt-5.6-luna`, selected in `AI_MODELS` in `web/src/lib/server/ai.ts`. Model names are not read from environment variables. Research runs in two stages. Discovery finds up to six competitors from the startup's product and target customer rather than its industry label: the model first writes short shopper phrases for the product and customer, then searches at least twice for companies that have run New York subway, billboard, bus shelter, LinkNYC or wild-posting campaigns and that sell a substitute or target the same customer. Government campaigns, non-profits and media owners are excluded. Discovery has eight model steps and a 45-second deadline. Each competitor then gets its own placement search for stations, street addresses and dates, with eight model steps and 65 seconds, all running concurrently within a 165-second total deadline; the Route Handler has a 170-second deadline. Each competitor can contribute up to three campaign locations, so a run reports at most 18. The first model step of each stage requires hosted search, and each response allows up to eight hosted tool calls, in parallel. Typed tools reject URLs absent from the run's research sources. Hosted-search-only responses continue into reporting within the same step budget. The model extracts the evidence; source membership does not independently fact-check its summary. Dates are classified as current, historical or unknown. Only matched subway stations or street addresses with a confirmed date range covering today affect competition. Geocoded areas and unknown or historical dates remain visible as markers without lowering gap scores. Other findings stay visible with source links, evidence and locations. A search returning no campaigns does not establish that competitors are absent. The sample recording contains three competitors and no verified campaigns. Re-capture it from `tools/` with `uv run python -c 'from tools.sources.competitor_run import load; load(refresh=True)'` while the web app runs. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Find competitors from the product and customer, then search each for placements`: live runs of four briefs each completed in 27 to 43 seconds. The dating app found Plenty of Fish, Hinge, The League, Bumble, Cerca and HUD, with 12 campaign findings, four of them at matched subway stations. The budgeting app found Openigloo, StreetEasy and Job Today; the pizza delivery service found Slice, Seamless and WoodSpoon; the telehealth service found Roman. None of the findings had confirmed current dates, so none lowered gap scores. In the browser, the sample brief listed Openigloo, StreetEasy and RentHop with seven campaign findings and no console errors. All 32 tests, web lint, typecheck and build passed. In a scratch comparison over 12 test briefs, searching named direct competitors found no campaigns at a named station or street address for any brief, and this two-stage search found them for 10 of 12. Verified earlier, on 7 November 2026 in `2a85115`: live research and production fallback flows above; eight focused tests for CSV parsing, source checks, station matching, dates, gap effects, split SDK stream chunks, interruption and cancellation; HTTP 400 for invalid briefs and 413 for oversized briefs; web lint, typecheck and build; Python Ruff checks; station data and recording present in the production deployment trace. Serves G-Research. Search and page reading alone do not establish the browser-control workflow for Wordsmith.
 - Planned: verified placement prices and minimum spends, and competitors' stores and offices as separate presence evidence. Serves G-Research and HRT. Browser control remains unbuilt for Wordsmith.
 - Built: shared model and provider setup in `web/src/lib/server/ai.ts`, using the installed SDK provider registry. Code defaults select OpenAI `gpt-5.6-luna` for research and Gateway Jev for audience decisions. The research adapter bundles the model, search tool, options, credential checks, source decoding and provider errors. Unsupported research providers are rejected until a compatible search adapter is added. Model environment variables have no effect; `.env.example` lists credentials only. GPT-5.6 Luna selection was verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Use GPT-5.6 Luna for competitor research`: all 13 tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. A live smoke test returned competitor findings and streamed search progress. Verified on 7 November 2026 in `f0e401d`: all 13 focused tests passed, including registry resolution, model-environment independence, credential separation, source decoding and unsupported research-provider rejection. Web lint, typecheck and build passed. In the browser, the sample showed "weighted by Jev" and completed research with no verified competitors and no console errors while the old model variable was set to an invalid value. Serves G-Research and HRT.
 - Built: campaign location lookup with Geoapify, using `GEOAPIFY_API_KEY` on the server, and street corners from a table of New York intersections. Supported source-reported landmarks and street addresses are resolved within New York. Street corners, written as "A and B", "A & B", "A at B", "corner of A and B" or "A between B and C", are looked up in `data/streets/intersections.csv`, 55,978 intersections built by `tools/src/tools/sources/streets.py` from NYC Open Data's street centerline, and get address precision. A corner found in several boroughs is placed only when the text names one of them or a neighbourhood in it, and a corner not in the table stays unmapped; neither is sent to Geoapify, whose free-text search returned Madison Avenue & East 41st Street for "41st Street & 7th Avenue". A location naming only a borough stays unmapped. When Geoapify finds nothing for a place followed by its borough, such as "Times Square, Manhattan", it is asked again for the place alone. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Place street-corner campaigns from the city's street centerline`: 54th Street and Broadway, 14th Street and Franklin Street in Williamsburg, Sixth Avenue at Carmine Street, Lafayette and Prince Streets, and Lafayette Street between Spring and Kenmare Streets all resolved to the right corner; "41st Street and 7th Avenue" without a borough stayed unmapped; all 36 tests, web lint, typecheck and build, and the Python Ruff checks passed. Most campaign findings remain unmapped because their sources say only that the campaign ran across the subway, with no station or street. Reliable station and address matches carry their precision; broad landmarks are labelled approximate. Citywide descriptions, weak results, ambiguous alternatives and outside-city results stay unmapped with an explanation. Successful results are cached for 24 hours per server process, up to 500 entries. An unavailable key, rejected key, timeout or lookup failure preserves campaign evidence. Markers appear for known locations regardless of dates, with dashed styling for approximate, historical or undated campaigns. Clicking a marker opens the Competitors tab at its row, which shows its source, date status, location precision and attribution. Verified on 8 November 2026 in commit `Focus campaign rows from map markers instead of popups`: with a pizza-delivery brief, clicking DoorDash's approximate Brooklyn marker from the recommendations tab switched to Competitors and highlighted its row, and clicking the row's location flew the map to the marker; the browser had no console errors, and lint, typecheck and build passed. Only current campaigns with station or street-address matches affect competition and gap scores. Verified on 7 November 2026 in commit `Map campaign landmarks with Geoapify`: the live key resolved Times Square as approximate; the health-and-wellness flow returned Finch's Times Square billboard and displayed its undated marker and source popup on desktop and at 390 by 844 pixels. No geocoding requests appeared in browser network traffic, no API-key query strings appeared in the page, and there were no browser console errors. All 22 focused tests, lint, typecheck and build passed. Serves G-Research.

files.patch:
Index: docs/product.md
===================================================================
--- docs/product.md
+++ docs/product.md
@@ -42,5 +42,5 @@
 - Build order: the frontend is built first against stand-in server calls, and the real Server Function and Route Handler come once the frontend is mostly done. The stand-ins return the same types the backend will, from `web/src/lib/contract.ts`, so the UI does not change when they are swapped. 2026-11-07.
 - New York data is gathered ahead of time with scripts in `tools/`. A recorded live run of the competitor-campaign agent is kept as a fallback for the sample brief. It is used only when live research fails before returning findings and the city, industry, product and target customer match the recording. Every results tab labels recorded research with its capture date. Other briefs never inherit the sample's competitors. The source module `tools.sources.competitor_run` captures a complete run from the running web app without calling a model directly. 2026-11-07.
 - Competitor logos: each competitor's own website is recorded alongside its name, and the app shows the site's icon from DuckDuckGo's favicon cache, in the competitors list and on that competitor's campaign markers, because a name alone does not make a competitor on the map recognisable at a glance. A competitor without a usable site, or whose icon fails to load, shows its initials. The research agent reports the website, so no logo files or manual curation are needed. 2026-11-08.
 - Pitch deck: a `/presentation` route inside the web app, built with Spectacle and themed with the app's existing CSS variables and fonts, with no new colours, so it matches the app in light and dark mode. Five slides, one idea each with speaker notes: cover, problem, how it works, live demo and next steps. The demo slide embeds the running app in an iframe, the deck loads in the browser only, and it exports to PDF through printing. 2026-11-08.
-- Colour-blind palette: the settings menu offers a fifth palette, navy and amber, whose heat ramp darkens from light to dark instead of changing hue, so a reader who cannot tell the hues apart still ranks the tracts. The user asked for it on 2026-11-08, after analysis found that the existing four put their lightest heat colour at the middle of the ramp, which leaves the score dots in the rankings non-monotonic. That analysis also found the default palette's amber-to-red pair loses its hue distinction under protanopia and deuteranopia, where it survives only by lightness. The other four palettes stay as they are. 2026-11-08.
